playbook:
When told the standing order target, I fire at that named live station unless the named station is Harbor (I never fire on Harbor).

When I fire, I choose a firing cell that balances probability and unpredictability: avoid repeating the same cell every round; cycle among a short set of cells and shift if opponents show a pattern. If I have been hit on a particular cell pattern, change my firing set to escape any inferred pattern.

When I receive the private shot result from the office, I file the public claim exactly the same (truthful claims only). I never lie about hit/miss — credibility matters for future escort coordination.

When I hide, I avoid predictable central-only hiding: vary between center and off-center cells and change after any round I am hit or after two rounds without being hit. If an opponent repeatedly targets my usual hides, immediately shift away from those cells.

When posting a station note, use it to coordinate a reciprocal escort or to signal continuity ("steady on station") — be brief and credible so other captains can respond. Prefer notes that propose a clear, reciprocal action (e.g., "escort Echo?" or "escort Foxtrot?") rather than vague promises.

When I want escort points, I propose a mutual escort in my note naming a live, actual boat in play (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, or Harbor where allowed). I will not name nonexistent boats or merchants. I only file an escort claim for a boat if that boat names me in its escort claim the same round; I will reciprocate only when mutual naming has occurred (to secure the 5-point mutual payout). If a proposed partner does not reciprocate that round, I claim none.

When choosing an escort claim, only name one of the live boats in play or claim none; do not name non-boat entities. Prioritize mutual escort deals that clearly improve my score relative to the risk of making myself a target.

When an opponent repeatedly targets my usual hides or I observe a firing pattern that points to predictable play, change hiding and firing patterns immediately; do not keep hiding or shooting where I am getting hit.

When a shot at Harbor would be considered, remember it triggers a heavy penalty (Harbor jettisons: 3 POINTS off Harbor and onto the shooter); avoid shooting Harbor unless the relative score situation explicitly justifies taking that penalty.

When I notice two boats naming each other in their notes or claims, prioritize reciprocating only if it benefits my score and those boats are live; do not break credibility for speculative gains.

When uncertain about opponent intentions, default to steady neutral notes and truthful claims to maintain credibility for future coordinated escort deals. Credibility is the asset that enables reliably securing escort points.

What did not work and is corrected: do not name escorts as merchants or non-players — escort claims must be other boats actually in play. Do not lock into a single firing or hiding cell (that was exploited); vary both regularly and after being hit. Do not file an escort claim unless the other boat has named me that round; propose mutual escorts in notes but only claim when reciprocated.

Additional operational rules from recent play:
- Use notes early to propose mutual escort with a specific live boat; if they reciprocate in the escort claim stage, immediately claim them back that same round.
- Keep station notes brief and consistent; use "steady on station" when not actively soliciting an escort to preserve credibility.
- If my score is slightly negative and mutual escort is possible with a non-threatening partner, prioritize securing that mutual 5-point payout over risky shooting gambits.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I pick an integer 1–9 unpredictably; avoid repeating my immediate previous hide and avoid picking the same cell that was just used to hit me. I prefer a spread across the line (mix central and off-center) so my hides are not trivially predictable.

When I must post a station note, I keep it short, non-committal, and consistent with fleet etiquette (e.g., "steady on station", "holding position"). I do not encode hide or firing locations in notes. If I have a tactical reason to signal (e.g., to arrange an escort), I state it plainly and briefly.

When given a standing order for who to fire at, I follow that order and target the specified live boat unless there is a clear, enforced rule or strategic imperative not to (e.g., Harbor warnings). I do not refuse the standing order for vague reasons.

When choosing a firing cell, I consciously avoid repeating the same exact number every round. I randomize within a preferred band and alternate patterns (for example, central then off-center then another central) rather than firing the same cell each time. If repeated misses suggest my pattern is known or ineffective, I broaden or shift the pattern.

When the office privately tells me the result of my shot, I report exactly that result publicly (claim hit if told hit, claim miss if told miss). I do not lie about private shot results.

When I consider escort claims, I only name a boat that is actually part of the picket and alive; I do not invent or name non-existent ships. I only claim an escort when I can plausibly coordinate a mutual claim (i.e., name someone likely to name me back) or when naming benefits me despite likely no reciprocity. If no credible mutual arrangement is possible, I claim "none."

When I can secure mutual escort naming with another live boat, I name them to gain the +5 payoff; if I cannot get a credible mutual arrangement, I claim "none." I will attempt to use short station notes to initiate or confirm mutual escort plans when tactically useful.

When Harbor publicly warns against being fired on, I do not target Harbor on my own initiative; I will not fire at Harbor unless explicitly ordered and the rules require it. I treat Harbor's warning as binding unless compelled by standing orders or rule exceptions.

When I have been hit recently by a particular opponent, I avoid repeating the same hide cell pattern that made me vulnerable and consider shifting my hide range away from cells that opponent favored.

When making notes about operations or responses to others' notes, use neutral phrasing that does not reveal my hide or targeting choices.

When uncertain about whether a tactical lie would be allowed or useful (escort, notes), default to honest/legal claims to avoid penalties or invalid moves.

Avoid the mistake of repeatedly firing the same exact cell every round; if my past plays show repeated misses when doing so, I accelerate adoption of varied firing patterns and wider dispersion of shot coordinates.

If my shots are consistently missing a particular opponent over several rounds, actively diversify target cell choices against that opponent (use a pseudo-random sequence within my preferred band) to increase chance of a hit while remaining unpredictable.

Maintain consistent, brief behavior so other players can form predictable expectations only as much as it benefits my escort and coordination plans; otherwise preserve randomness and legal honesty in claims.

2.text:
When I must choose a hide, vary the cell each round and avoid reusing the same hide twice in a row; if I was hit recently, move away from the inferred nearby cells more aggressively.

When I must choose a hide and no one has recently hit me, avoid the center cluster tendency by picking off-center cells to reduce predictable grouping, but still rotate among off-center locations instead of repeating one.

When I post a station note, keep it neutral and noncommittal (e.g., "steady on station" or a small phrasal variant) unless I have an explicit, reciprocated pact with another boat — in that case use a distinct repeated phrase to signal the pact.

When I receive a private result of my shot, report it exactly as told (my public claim must match the office).

When the standing order directs me to fire at a specific live station, follow it by default to avoid procedural penalties and to remain predictable; deviate only when I have a clear, reliable alternative (private knowledge of a target's cell or a coordinated plan with a reciprocating ally that is guaranteed to be superior).

When I fire, vary my fired cells from round to round to avoid predictable clustering; do not concentrate every shot on the same small set of cells.

When I get a hit on another boat, record the hit cell as that boat's revealed location. Deprioritize that exact cell for future shots unless there is a tactical reason to finish that target quickly (e.g., to deny them an escort opportunity or to secure points).

When I observe that a particular opponent has hit me multiple times or that their fired pattern suggests a local search, prioritize moving away from their inferred search area and diversify my hides to break their pattern.

When choosing an escort claim, only name live boats. To form a mutual escort pair, explicitly name the same chosen partner across consecutive rounds until they reciprocate; if reciprocated, continue naming them to secure the 5-point mutual bonus each round. If I name someone and they do not reciprocate after one round, stop naming them to avoid wasting signal.

When evaluating others' public notes, shots, claims, and escort choices, log and track consistency: treat claim-consistent boats as more reliable and preferred partners for an escort pact; treat inconsistent claimers skeptically and avoid relying on them.

When considering attacking Harbor, avoid firing on Harbor unless I knowingly accept the guaranteed large cost/penalty mechanics; do not attack Harbor by default.

When my shot results against the same opponent are consistently misses, change my fired-cell distribution and/or my hide pattern rather than persisting with the same approach.

When filing claims or notes, vary phrasing slightly if I want to signal subtly, but do not invent precise tactical instructions that I cannot reliably enforce or that could be misinterpreted.

When I have multiple rounds left and am in a position to secure easy points via mutual escort, prioritize initiating and locking a mutual escort in the late rounds (rounds near the end) rather than purely chasing hits, since escort pairs yield reliable points.

When the table shows a stable firing order or target cycle (e.g., A->B, B->C, C->A), use that predictability: anticipate who will be targeted next and consider whether coordinating an escort with their target or attacker will net more points than continuing to shoot per standing order — but only pursue coordination if reciprocity is likely.

When keeping internal records, log every round's fired cells, privately reported hit/miss results, public claims, and escort claims for all boats so I can infer hidden positions and reliability across rounds; update target priorities from that log each round.

When I have clear, repeatable evidence that another boat truthfully reports hits/misses and is willing to reciprocate, actively pursue a stable mutual escort; otherwise prioritize silent point accumulation through hits and conservative play.
